text:
carmen: heads-up: ran into a weird one when consuming our starter package from a pnpm monorepo + Next (nodenext) app. generics collapse to `any` only when the consumer uses path aliases + pnpm workspace. CJS and single-package installs are fine. anyone seen pnpm/workspace-specific d.ts resolution quirks?

itao: interesting. pnpm symlinks change how the TS resolver walks node_modules. do you have `preserveSymlinks` set in node or tsconfig? pnpm creates symlinks which can make TS pick up a different package root and different typeRoots.

carmen: no special preserveSymlinks. repo is monorepo with workspace: ["packages/*"], starter package published to local registry for testing. package.json exports: { "import": "./dist/esm/index.mjs", "require": "./dist/cjs/index.cjs" }, types: "dist/types/index.d.ts". We also have path aliases in the consumer: "@lib/*": ["../packages/lib/src/*"].

felix: path aliases in consumer can interact poorly: tsc will resolve the alias to source files and then prefer TS source over the published d.ts for that package. if the consumer's paths shadow the published types, you can end up with mixed declaration resolution and weird widenings (especially if the source has `any` in impl).

nora: also check top-level `typeRoots` and `types` in tsconfig of consumer. pnpm hoists some packages, and TS might pick up a different @types package causing a different lib target. subtle, but I've seen changes in lib.dom or esnext types change inference.

carmen: hmmm. the symptom is specific: exported overloaded function shows correct overloads if imported directly from node_modules (after we copy dist/types into dist/esm as index.mjs.d.ts), but when consumer uses a path alias to point to our package source (for faster dev), the editor shows single (x: any) => any.

itao: that suggests the consumer's path alias is importing your src (ts) not the built ESM entry. If your source implementation uses `any` internally, that will affect the inferred signature in editor. quick repro: change impl to `function foo<T>(x: T): T { return x as T }` and see if alias import keeps generics.

felix: also check if project references are used. In a composite setup, declaration emit and reference resolution can differ between packages. If the consumer uses the source and your package uses `composite: true` + `declarationMap`, tsc can cross-project reference and pick up a different signature surface.

nora: small checklist:
- avoid `any` in public impls (use generic impl or cast at boundary)
- prefer `dist/types/index.d.ts` and postbuild copy into esm/cjs entry names for published package
- avoid publishing path aliases; consumers should import published package names, not workspace source, if you want the packaged d.ts surface
- if you want path-alias dev flow, add a local tsconfig paths override that points to your built dist (not src)

carmen: good points. i want to keep DX fast (edit src directly) but not break type expectations. maybe we can adjust our starter README to recommend using the dist build with `pnpm link` or adjusting paths to point to `dist` during local dev.

itao: alternative: generate a small types-only package (`@redwood/starter-types`) that consumers can reference in tsconfig `paths` during dev; keeps source hot-reload for code but stabilizes types. a bit extra infra but robust.

felix: one more gotcha: tsserver running in the consumer workspace may have a different TS version than the package's compiled d.ts. ensure `typescript` is pinned consistently or enable `useWorkspaceTsdk` appropriately. Mismatched TS versions sometimes behave differently for overload resolution and `unknown`/`any` inference.

carmen: also saw a weird case where `typesVersions` got ignored until i bumped package version. had to publish a prerelease to force the consumer to resolve the conditional mapping. is that expected?

nora: that can happen because the consumer's resolver caches package metadata in the pnpm store. bumping the version or clearing node_modules resolves it. Not ideal in tight dev loops.

bot-ci: Note: opened issue #601 "starter: monorepo path-alias + pnpm -> collapsed overloads in consumer editor" and created branch starter/601-types-workflow.

carmen: plan: 1) change visible impls in starter to generic-style (no impl `any`), 2) add a postbuild to copy dist/types to both esm/cjs names, 3) add a short dev note for pnpm/paths explaining 'if you point consumer to src via paths, prefer pointing to dist types or use a types-only package'. i'll open a PR and add a CI tsd test that imports via pnpm workspace.

itao: +1. if you include a tiny example `pnpm-workspace` consumer in the repo for maintainers to reproduce quickly, that saves time when testing future changes.

felix: also add a note about `tsserver` version pinning in the contributor docs. that was a pain point for new hires.

carmen: thanks all. i'll draft the PR and ping eng-devex. will paste links here when ready. :sparkles:
